settings.editor: A small restaurant on Harbour Lane, cooking over oak and beech. The menu follows the market and changes most weeks.

There is one oven and no gas line. Bread, vegetables, fish and meat all take their turn over the same embers, which is why the menu is short and why the room smells the way it does.

We buy from eleven growers and one fishing boat, and we write the menu after they have told us what they have.

settings.title: Four dishes people come back for

settings.editor: We hold half the room for walk-ins. For the other half, call us or send a line, and we will confirm the same day.
Birthdays, rehearsal dinners, the evening after the conference. One table, one menu cooked for everyone at once, and the room to yourselves.

settings.title: “The best thing I ate this year was a leek. I have thought about it every week since.”
